case_name: Acit Central Circle-1 , Jaipur vs Mahendra Kumar Agarwal, Jaipur
facts_of_case: Assessment year 2017-18. Revenue appealed against order of CIT(A)-4, Jaipur dated 10-02-2022.

legal_principles.principle: A transaction cannot be treated as non-genuine for want of details which are not required to obtain and keep as per the law.
legal_principles.held: It is admitted fact that each transaction should be analyzed with the point of view of the businessman, generally prevailing practice in the trade and its acceptability in the eye of law.
cited_cases: R.B. Jessaram Fatehchand (Sugar Dept.) v/s Commissioner of Income Tax [1970] 75 ITR 33 (Bombay)

legal_principles.principle: Making some sales in cash is no ground for rejecting the books of account.
legal_principles.held: There should be some material that cash sales made by assessee either on account of sale on a lower price or sale made out of the material which is not shown in the books of account.
cited_cases: ACIT Circle-1 Jaipur Vs M/s Uttam Chand Deshraj (ITAT Jaipur Bench ITA No 419/JP/2010)

legal_principles.principle: So long as the availability of stock is there and there is nothing adverse against the cash memos issued by the assessee, such cash sales cannot be doubted.
legal_principles.held: We find that so long as the availability of stock in there and there is nothing adverse against the cash memos issued by the assessee, such cash sales cannot be doubted.
cited_cases: Kishore Jeram Bhai Khaniya, Proprietor, M/s Poonam Enterprises v. ITO ITA No. 1220/Del/2011 (ITAT Delhi Judgement dated 13.05.2014)

use_for_drafting: Drafting an appeal against the order of CIT(A)
Responding to a revenue appeal in income tax matters
Guidance on burden of proof in tax disputes
